findings.excerpt:
theorem colimit_ι_nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison (i : Set.Ici i0) :
    colimit.ι ((restricted S i0 U0).rightOp ⋙ SheafedSpace.Γ) i ≫
        nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison S i0 m U0 =
findings.problem: This is the defining coprojection law for the comparison map, in the same role as `colimit.ι_desc`. It has no `reassoc` companion and no simp attribute. Its consumers therefore re-associate by hand. `originalStage_nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison` (lines 78–97) uses a three-step `calc` with `Category.assoc _ _ _` and a `congrArg (eqToHom … ≫ ·)`, which is exactly what `_assoc` would do. The examples file does the same with a manual `(Category.assoc …).trans hleg`. `nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison` is also a plain `def`, so `simp` cannot see through it. Without a rule, any `colimit.ι … ≫ nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison …` term inside a longer composite has no canonical rewrite.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`, or at least `@[reassoc]`. The generated `colimit_ι_nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison_assoc` replaces the `calc` steps at lines 78–91 and the manual `Category.assoc` in `SheafCohomologyExamples/NativeAdditiveCylinderSections.lean`. If `simp` is also wanted, the right-hand side is a closed normal form in terms of `Γ.map` of the restricted-cone projection followed by `eqToHom`. The attribute does not need to touch `restrict_Γ_obj`. The existing sibling `colimit_ι_nativeAdditiveGlobalSectionsComparison` has the same gap, so it should be fixed in the same way.
findings.benefit: Composites that start with the coprojection can be simplified directly instead of being re-associated by hand. `originalStage_nativeAdditiveCylinderSectionsComparison` would shrink from a manual `calc` to roughly a `reassoc`/`simp` call plus the `hcomponent` step. Later lemmas in the cylinder-naturality files would also get a canonical rewrite for the coprojection. The `…_assoc` form is the standard Mathlib convention for such `ι ≫ desc`-style lemmas.
